cover_headline: Indian Battery Makers Face Up to 61% Cost Gap With China, NETRA Study Finds
facts: Indian battery component makers face a cost disadvantage of 18% to 61% against landed Chinese prices, worst in synthetic graphite anodes at 61%
Building an anode plant in India costs 425% more than in China, and Indian firms borrow at 8.5–16% against about 3.1% in China
China, the study notes, supplied 99% of the world's LFP cathode material and 90% of anode material in 2025

quote.text: The cost data in this report comes from Indian companies that are building or planning these plants, and it shows that the gap has a different cause in each component. A flat incentive would overpay some producers and underpay others.
quote.speaker: Debi Prasad Dash

end.headline: Indian Battery Makers Face Up to 61% Cost Gap With China, NETRA Study Finds
end.line: The NETRA study for the Heavy Industries Ministry prices the disadvantage component by component and offers three subsidy options, up to a 50% capital subsidy.
